notes.s: After the stadiums, he wants the small facts of one person's ordinary day.
notes.t: Lead single of Map of the Soul: Persona, April 2019, with Halsey. The Korean title means a poem for small things, and the song is a direct answer to the scale of their own earlier records: world peace and grand order get waved off in the rap verse so he can ask what made your day good. It entered the Hot 100 at number eight and they performed it on Saturday Night Live the same month. The pastel sixties-musical staging made it the most mainstream-looking thing they had released, and ARMY reads the line about lowering his eyes to meet hers as addressed to the fandom rather than to a girlfriend.
k: 맞추다 is to align one thing to another, and 눈을 맞추다 on its own is to make eye contact. The lyric bends it: he is high up now and wants to bring himself down to where her eyes are. Fans translate it both as wanting to look her in the eye and as wanting to lower himself to her level, and the song supports both at once.

Icarus's wings, inverted. In the myth the wings melt because he flies at the sun; here the wings are a gift from her and he aims away from the sun and toward the person. It answers the WINGS album era, where flight was always a fall waiting to happen.

The same adjective twice, once plain and once negated, with -게 만들다, to make something become a certain way. The template is portable: A를 B하지 않게 만들다, to make A stop being B. The -버리다 on the end marks it as done irreversibly, so she did not just change his view, she finished it.
툭 까놓고 말할게 / 힘이 들어가기도 했어

Two idioms in one breath. 툭 까놓고 말하다 is to peel the thing open and say it flat out, from 까다 to peel, and it signals a confession is coming. 힘이 들어가다 is literally strength entering, used for tensing up or overdoing it, the thing a coach tells an athlete to stop doing.
